themes.label: Complete
themes.rationale: The short funerary formula is preserved in its entirety, containing the name, age, and closing salutation.

rationale: This is a brief funerary inscription from Alexandria dating to the 1st or 2nd century AD. It follows a standard Roman-period formula: the name of the deceased in the vocative (Achilles), the age at death (43 years), and the valedictory command 'eupsychei', which translates to 'be of good cheer' or 'farewell', intended to comfort the soul of the departed.
